entries.summary: November 23 05:21 EST: Bearish elevated downside risk persists for November 23–25 despite strengthening premarket relief rally. Nasdaq-100 futures reportedly +3.3% at 08:51 GMT and Barron's reports SOXX premarket >6%; both remain indicative, not confirmed US cash-market breadth or sustained reversal. Taiwan intervention is already incorporated in Open Watch; no independently verified new regime-changing catalyst. Friday's SOX/QQQ liquidation, extreme volatility and forthcoming inflation data retain downside risk. Paired current Treasury yields, VXN/VIX, FedWatch and matched oil remain unverified.

editorial.marketOverview: Nasdaq and semiconductor risk remains elevated following Friday's unusually deep selloff. The Monday premarket bounce is increasingly broad across index futures and semiconductor ETFs, but has not yet established an actual US cash-session reversal. Positioning stress and event risk remain dominant.
editorial.whatChanged: Since the prior 03:36 EST assessment, a secondary Reuters-attributed 08:51 GMT observation placed Nasdaq-100 futures at +3.3%, above the earlier +3.02% 02:29 EST Reuters indication; these timestamps are not synchronized. Barron's separately reports SOXX more than 6% higher premarket. Open Watch refreshed at 2026-11-23T09:52:52+00:00 with 175 events; Taiwan stabilization is already known, not a new catalyst.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The premarket chip rebound reduces immediate downside momentum and supports an oversold relief rally, but does not yet justify upgrading the three-session bias. Friday's historical SOX underperformance, breadth damage, elevated volatility and deleveraging remain adverse. US cash confirmation and rate-volatility alignment are essential.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday: an opening relief rally is plausible but vulnerable to fading, particularly after flash PMI data. Tuesday: test whether chip leadership survives and whether Dell earnings and consumer confidence reinforce demand. Wednesday: PCE/GDP and Fed communications can reprice yields and interrupt the rebound; the distribution of outcomes remains wide.
editorial.bullCase: SOXX's indicated >6% premarket rise and roughly 3% Nasdaq futures recovery show appetite for beaten-down AI exposure. Sustained US cash semiconductor outperformance, better breadth and declining volatility would turn a squeeze into a credible stabilization phase.
editorial.bearCase: A failed cash-session rebound, renewed semiconductor relative weakness or hawkish inflation/rate repricing could resume forced selling. Geopolitical oil risk and uncertainty around AI capital spending magnify the downside if volatility remains high.
editorial.watchNext: Verify cash QQQ/Nasdaq and SOX/SMH at matched timestamps; watch NYSE/Nasdaq breadth, VXN/VIX, 10Y and 2Y yields with correct units, FedWatch and matched Brent/WTI contracts. Check flash PMI release versus consensus, HPE and Dell results, and Wednesday PCE/GDP; do not treat expected catalyst impacts as realized moves.
